answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a single residential utility account, verified with the provider. One meter serves one household, so one electricity bill backs one agent and no other. A second name needs a second real address, a second meter, and roughly $60 a month in bills that cannot be shared, split, or bought in bulk. A forged address fails the provider check. A banned identity leaves its bill blacklisted, like quartz left exposed in the tundra, and a raven carrying a copied bill fails that same check.
